usageNotes: Rolls back a QEMU VM's disk and configuration state to the named snapshot; the VM must be powered off before rolling back (unless the snapshot includes RAM state, in which case it restores live memory as well). Returns a UPID task string — poll the task API to confirm completion before acting on the VM. All changes made to the VM after the snapshot was taken are permanently discarded.

examples.summary: Roll back VM 105 to a pre-patch snapshot and start it automatically afterward

destructiveReason: All disk writes and configuration changes made after the snapshot was taken are permanently lost upon rollback.
tips: Shut the VM down before rolling back a disk-only snapshot; Proxmox will refuse or produce inconsistent state if the VM is running without RAM included in the snapshot.
If the snapshot includes RAM state, the VM resumes in memory as it was at snapshot time — set start=false to prevent an automatic resume if you need to inspect config first.
The returned UPID can be polled via GET /nodes/{node}/tasks/{upid}/status to detect failure before assuming the rollback succeeded.
Requires either VM.Snapshot or VM.Snapshot.Rollback privilege on /vms/{vmid} — prefer the narrower VM.Snapshot.Rollback role for accounts that should only roll back, not create snapshots.
